title: Listening to Events with v-on
description: Learn the basics of binding DOM events and calling methods.

slides.title: v-on: The Event Listener
slides.content:
# Listening to DOM Events

To make your app interactive, you need to respond to user actions like clicks, typing, or mouse movements. Vue provides the **`v-on`** directive for this.

```html
<button v-on:click="doSomething">Click me</button>
```

When the button is clicked, Vue calls the `doSomething` method (or executes the inline expression).

**Shorthand**: `@click="doSomething"`

slides.title: Method Handlers vs Inline Handlers
slides.content:
## Two Ways to Handle Events

1. **Method handler** – point to a method defined in `methods`.
   ```html
   <button @click="greet">Greet</button>
   ```

2. **Inline handler** – write a small JavaScript expression.
   ```html
   <button @click="count++">Increment</button>
   ```

Use method handlers for logic that needs access to `this` or is reusable. Use inline handlers for simple expressions.
